title: Azure DevOps, Bicep & Container Apps
exp: Modern Azure infrastructure deployment uses Bicep, Azure Container Apps (ACA) with KEDA autoscaling, and Azure Pipelines / GitHub Actions.
pts: **Azure Bicep vs ARM Templates:** concise syntax, type safety, modular resource definitions (`module`).
**Azure Container Apps (ACA):** serverless container hosting powered by AKS, Envoy, and KEDA (Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling).
**KEDA Trigger Scaling:** scaling container replicas from 0 to N based on Azure Service Bus queue depth or Event Hubs lag.
**Azure Key Vault Integration:** referencing secrets in Bicep / ACA via Key Vault secret URIs.
pr: Write a modular Bicep template for App Service + Key Vault
Configure KEDA Azure Service Bus queue scale rule in ACA

r: Deep mechanics of Azure DevOps, Bicep & Container Apps under concurrent execution.
Always design for idempotency, cancellation propagation, and thread safety.
Memory allocation spikes or CPU bound thread starvation.
Use profiling tools to measure actual baseline allocation before optimizing.
Balancing developer velocity with operational maintenance complexity.
Favor simple, well-tested modular architectures over premature complexity.

qa.q: When should you choose Azure Container Apps (ACA) over Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Choose ACA when running microservices or background workers needing container isolation and KEDA event-driven autoscaling (down to 0) without managing Kubernetes control planes, ingress controllers, or node pools.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Message brokers persist events to partitioned append-only logs or in-memory queues, enabling distributed pub/sub with consumer groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Poison pill messages without dead-letter queues (DLQ) block partition processing and trigger infinite retry loops.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Partitioned event streaming (Kafka) guarantees order per key at scale, but partition rebalancing incurs consumer pause latency.

qa.q: How does KEDA autoscale Azure Container Apps based on queue depth?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** KEDA monitors Azure Service Bus queue lengths. When unconsumed message count exceeds threshold, KEDA signals ACA to spin up additional container instances dynamically, scaling back to zero when idle.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Signals build a fine-grained reactive dependency graph. When a signal value changes, only dependent view nodes are scheduled for DOM updating.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Mutating signal values inside effects without untracked() causes infinite change detection loops and browser freeze.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Signals provide predictable synchronous reactivity without Zone.js overhead, but require adapting existing RxJS-heavy codebases.

interviewPlaybook.openingScript: In enterprise cloud environments, Azure DevOps, Bicep & Container Apps must be designed with fault tolerance, zero-downtime deployment pipelines, and explicit security boundaries.
interviewPlaybook.incidentStory: A regional outage threatened pipeline ingestion availability when a dependency failed around Azure DevOps, Bicep & Container Apps. Using infrastructure-as-code and automated failover, I implemented circuit breaking and fallback routing, keeping client payload ingestion at 99.99% availability.
